coverage_of_risk.rationale: No tests exist in app/, and the riskiest logic (sorting, filtering, pagination, URL state, species mapping) has no coverage beyond the frozen acceptance suite.

evidence: app/ — no test files, so no low-value tests to maintain
signal_to_noise.rationale: No tests means no noise, but also nothing earning its keep; per the rubric a no-tests codebase anchors at 3.

findings.issue: No test runner, no test script, and zero test files in the entire app; ~850 significant LOC of pure logic ship with no safety net once the acceptance suite evolves
findings.suggestion: Add vitest (or node:test) with a unit suite over the exported pure functions: humanize, englishName, latestEnglishFlavor, speciesFromPokemonList/speciesFromEntries, sortRows, buildUrl

findings.issue: All rendering is escapeHtml-guarded innerHTML string concatenation; removing a single escapeHtml call (e.g. on a humanized name like Farfetch'd) breaks markup or introduces injection, and nothing in app/ would fail
findings.suggestion: At minimum a unit test that every card/row renderer escapes a hostile name; ideally move to DOM APIs or a tiny h() helper so escaping is structural

findings.issue: sortRows encodes four fiddly rules (null-last in both directions, level-up default sort, name tie-break, aria-sort flip) with no unit tests
findings.suggestion: Table-driven unit tests for each rule using hand-built MoveRow fixtures

findings.issue: Alternate-form exclusion (id > 10000), Map dedup and hidden-flag merging in speciesFromEntries are untested; a refactor to name-matching would silently drop or duplicate species
findings.suggestion: Unit tests with mixed species/variety IDs, duplicates and hidden flags

findings.issue: Pagination clamping and buildUrl's omit-defaults rule are only exercised by the happy-path acceptance tests; deep links like /?page=999 or ?q= are untested
findings.suggestion: Unit tests on buildUrl (each param omitted when default) and on the clamp logic for page beyond range and zero matches

findings.issue: Path-traversal guard and the < escaping of the injected __API_BASE_URL__ script are security-relevant and untested
findings.suggestion: A few node:test cases against the server: GET /../etc/passwd, GET /%2e%2e/, and API base containing '</script>'

findings.issue: renderToken/gameRequest stale-render guards are concurrency-critical and untestable by the sequential acceptance suite; removing them causes intermittent cross-page render bleed
findings.suggestion: Keep the guards; add a unit test that a superseded render's promise does not write to main (inject isActive false)

findings.issue: apiFetch promise cache deletes entries only on failure; no test pins the 'failed request is retried next call' behaviour
findings.suggestion: Unit test with a mocked fetch that fails once then succeeds

findings.issue: methodRank ordering (Level Up, Machine, Egg, Tutor, then others alphabetically) has a subtle sort branch with no direct test
findings.suggestion: Table-driven unit test over a shuffled set of method names

summary: The app contains no tests of any kind — no runner configured, no script, no files — so the only protection for ~850 LOC of dense filtering, sorting, pagination and string-templating logic is the frozen acceptance suite. The risky logic is cleanly factored into exported pure functions, which makes adding a small vitest/node:test unit suite cheap and leaves the omission hard to justify. As a PR this is a reject until at least the data layer and sort/URL-state helpers have regression coverage.
